title: Global LNG Supply Crunch Set to Spill Into 2027 | OilPrice.com
text:
Iran War Is Pushing Record Numbers of Fuel Tankers Into Crude Trade

The global market for liquefied natural gas will remain relatively tight next year, Malaysia’s state energy major Petronas has forecast, noting the continued supply disruption in the Middle East, which will keep prices for LNG elevated.

“Looking into next year, we expect market conditions to remain relatively tight, which could continue to support LNG prices until more supply becomes available,” said Petronas executive VP and chief executive for gas and maritime business, Datuk Adif Zulkifli, as quoted by Bernama.

The supply situation, however, will depend on several factors, including how long the war in the Middle East continues and the speed of LNG supply growth globally. This growth has been accelerating because of the war, as importers look for alternatives to Qatari and Emirati liquefied gas.

Qatar has struggled to restore flows of LNG, unlike oil exporters, which have managed to boost their exports with ship-to-ship transfers. There were earlier reports about LNG ship-to-ship transfers as well, outside the Strait of Hormuz, but it appears the practice has not become as popular with LNG exporters as it has with oil exporters.

U.S. LNG exports have been running at all-time highs this year, and the trend will likely extend into next year as well. Africa is meanwhile turning into another major source of liquefied gas, with exports of the superchilled fuel from sub-Saharan Africa specifically seen soaring by 175% by 2034, thanks to development of new projects in Mozambique, Nigeria, Senegal, and Mauritania.

Over the short term, gas demand growth could weaken, according to Rystad Energy, which cited the development of El Niño and the warmer weather it may bring. A milder-than-normal winter in key LNG-consuming regions of the Northern Hemisphere could curb heating demand and ease pressure on LNG prices. Meanwhile, persistently elevated LNG prices could encourage greater reliance on coal-fired power generation, particularly in Asia.
